summary: Point Stuart Light: a 1915 electric light and siren on the west side of Angel Island in San Francisco Bay, marking Raccoon Strait. Now inactive; site and tower closed.

notes_for_editor: Left out of the story: (1) the record's deactivation year 1960 (Wikidata). No source read dates the light going out; the Angel Island Conservancy's 1960 date is for the new Point Blunt station. (2) Coordinates 37.861063, -122.446171 come from OpenStreetMap; no source read gives coordinates. Rowlett and the Conservancy place the light on the west or north-west side of Angel Island about 800 m north of Point Knox, and the position was not changed. The record's status note says the coordinates may be unusable; a check against the Light List or a survey is advised. (3) Record characteristic Fl R 2.5s (from ENC) is not confirmed by any source read. (4) USLHS place page: Existing: No, Location: Angel Island; no keeper roster. (5) Newspapers: Chronicling America California papers searched for 'Point Stuart' 1900-1920 and for 'Point Stuart' with 'Angel Island' 1912-1917; the hits did not concern the light; none used. (6) Not used: the 1936 Bulletin account of Albert Joost, who was keeper of Southampton Shoal, not Point Stuart; the 1925 Bulletin passage about an 'Angel Island Light' keeper striking the fog bell by hand, which is not tied to Point Stuart. (7) The 1915 Commissioner's lists name Point Stuart among Pacific lights (printed pp. 38 and 40, scan pp. 43 and 45); OCR is garbled there; not needed. (8) Lighthouse Digest database entry for the light returned HTTP 503 and was not read. (9) Marin County is not stated in any source read, and the story does not name it. (10) A second station file exists at data/stations/ca/us-ca-point-stuart-2.json; not read or compared. (11) The record's lighthouse 'arlhs' and 'uscg' ids were not checked. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Point Blunt date disagrees: the Conservancy says the new facility completed in 1960, Rowlett says the Coast Guard station was constructed in 1961; the story states both. The 1916 Bulletin 'PDF p. 1' and the 1915 Commissioner printed pp. 8 and 100 were confirmed by corpus page lookups. The record's 1960 deactivation value still has no source for the light going out.
